entries.title: While the Bears rested, the NFC North proved nasty
entries.summary: <p>A week ago, Ben Johnson looked at the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ bye week as a challenge — a time for the coach to figure out how to improve everything from run-game explosiveness to quarterback consistency to defensive oomph.</p><p>“There's a great opportunity at hand just to look at these first nine games and come away with what we're doing well and what we can lean on going into the last stretch of the season,” he said. “And certainly some areas of improvement that we need to get better at.”</p><p>What went unspoken was exactly why the Bears needed to be so sharp. Despite going 7-2 in their first nine games, they were far from the runaway favorite to win the NFC North. The Bears’ division is the best in the NFL, and by the end of the season could be considered one of the best in league history. If the Bears played in the NFC South, they’d be in first place by three games. In the NFC North, they’re in third place.</p><p>How nasty is the NFC North? The Bears didn’t play a game Sunday and fell four spots in the NFC’s playoff picture. Even with the Lions likely losing star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a knee injury, the division is a gauntlet. The Vikings’ dominance of the Packers at Lambeau Field reinforced as much.</p><p>Johnson is chasing perfection out of necessity. Without it, the Bears could miss the postseason. They are one of three NFC North teams sitting at 7-2 after Sunday, with the Packers at 6-4.</p><p>“There's a certain standard that we want to hit week-in and week-out,” he said. “I think the good teams, even when they get victories, if they don't hit those benchmarks then that leaves some more to be desired. And I felt that from our crew, which is a good thing.</p><p>“I think that's the next evolution of this team, not just that we win but the manner in which we play."</p><p>After they beat the Seahawks, the Bears spent a week being <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/12/catch-22-bears-cris-collinsworth-mike-tomlin-built-go-far-caleb-williams-ben-johnson-bye-week" >touted by national talking heads </a>as a Super Bowl favorite. A week later, while the Bears were busy winning ugly against the Buccaneers, the Packers inherited that mantle when they thumped the defending AFC champion Patriots in New England.</p><p>This week, it will be the Vikings, who emerged as the league’s big winner of the weekend by <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/vikings-beat-packers-30-10-in-kirk-cousins-return-jordan-love-is-sacked-8-times" >dispatching the Packers 30-10</a> at Lambeau Field. The Bears, by contrast, lost 31-7 in the same place a month ago.</p><p>Quarterback Kirk Cousins steadied the ship Sunday, five days after being traded by the Raiders and six days after Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz looked lost in a “Monday Night Football” debacle against the Bills. The Vikings’ defense continued to do what it’s done all season — perform like the best single unit on either side of the ball in the NFL.</p><p>The Vikings tortured Jordan Love, sacking the Packers quarterback eight times. They forced four turnovers — one interception and a whopping three fumbles. The last time the Vikings had eight sacks and four takeaways in one game was 37 years ago.</p><p>That blitzing formula worked for the Vikings against the Bears in Week 2 — and for the Buccaneers a week ago. While NFL teams figure to blitz Bears quarterback Caleb Williams even more going forward, no one does it as well as Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores.</p><p>Cousins was solid Sunday, throwing for 207 yards and two touchdowns. More importantly, star receiver Justin Jefferson looked far more comfortable with Cousins that he did Wentz or Kyler Murray. His 13 targets were the most he’s had all season, while his 74 receiving yards were his most in five weeks.</p><p>The Vikings, though, don’t even sit in first place in the North anymore. The Lions do — but their long flight home from Germany after a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/lions-patriots-munich-drake-maye-aiden-hutchinson-injuries" >35-10 win against the Patriots </a>was undoubtedly muted.</p><p>Hutchinson hurt his knee while celebrating a sack of the Patriots’ Drake Maye, who was subsequently knocked out of the game. The Lions planned for him to get further examinations when they landed back in America but reportedly fear that he’ll be lost for the season. It was reminiscent of former Bears linebacker Lamarr Houston tearing his ACL while celebrating a sack of the Patriots’ backup quarterback in a 2014 game in which the Bears were trailing by 25 points.</p><p>The timing is notable for the Lions — and the Bears. Losing Hutchinson just days after the NFL’s trade deadline would leave a gaping hole in a Lions defense that was suspect to begin with. Without him, their defense isn’t Super Bowl quality.</p><p>The Bears could take advantage soon, too — the Lions play the Buccaneers next week before hosting the Bears on Thanksgiving Day. Johnson has never beaten his former team. The Bears need a divisional win desperately, having lost to both the Packers and Vikings earlier this season.</p><p>The Thanksgiving game starts a run of four divisional games over the Bears’ final seven contests. Every game, every detail has a chance to tilt the division.</p><p>The Bears learned that Sunday without even taking the field.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/vikings-beat-packers-30-10-in-kirk-cousins-return-jordan-love-is-sacked-8-times" >Vikings beat Packers 30-10 in Kirk Cousins’ return; Jordan Love is sacked 8 times</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/lions-patriots-munich-drake-maye-aiden-hutchinson-injuries" >Lions rout Patriots 35-10 in Munich; Aidan Hutchinson reportedly out for the season</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/bears-next-opponent-saints-fall-to-the-panthers-20-17" >Bears’ next opponent: Saints fall to the Panthers 20-17</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Lions rout Patriots 35-10 in Munich; Aidan Hutchinson reportedly out for the season
entries.summary: <p>MUNICH — Amon-Ra St. Brown wore lederhosen, carried a German flag onto the field, and then went out and scored two touchdowns.</p><p>Talk about a homecoming.</p><p>The German-speaking St. Brown, whose mother is from Leverkusen, said it's been a trip he'll "never forget."</p><p>St. Brown caught two touchdown passes and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and two scores in a 35-10 win over the New England Patriots, who lost quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury on their opening drive Sunday.</p><p>"Being in Germany, number one, was a blessing, it's been amazing," St. Brown said. "But being able to win like that — with the guys, my teammates in front of the fans here in Germany, it's like a dream come true."</p><p>The Lions (7-2) have won five straight games but also lost edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who hurt his right knee while celebrating the sack that knocked Maye out of the game. A person familiar with the situation later told The Associated Press that Hutchinson's injury was season-ending.</p><p>"Any time you lose a player like that and you don't know the entirety of it ... it hurts a little bit," Lions coach Dan Campbell said.</p><p>Jared Goff threw three touchdown passes, along with two interceptions, completing 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards.</p><p>St. Brown caught a 56-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter to give Detroit a 7-3 lead. And his 28-yard TD reception — after teammates pushed him over the goal line in a scrum with Patriots defenders — made it 28-3 in the third quarter.</p><p>St. Brown, who wore lederhosen for his arrival to the stadium, charged onto the field carrying a German flag. St. Brown and his two brothers spent many summers in their childhood visiting the country.</p><p>In between St. Brown's scores, Goff found Isaac TeSlaa for a 12-yard touchdown pass and a 14-3 lead after a 97-yard drive, and Gibbs ran it in from 5 yards one play after he rumbled down the sideline for a 50-yard reception.</p><p>Gibbs added a 28-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to make it 35-10. He is the first NFL player since Priest Holmes in 2002 to produce more than 150 yards rushing with two rushing touchdowns and at least 95 yards receiving in a game, the Lions said.</p><p>Gibbs caught seven passes for 99 yards. St. Brown finished with four receptions for 98 yards.</p><p>The Patriots (5-5) have lost back-to-back games and three of four.</p><p>Tommy DeVito completed 12 of 24 for 81 yards with one interception and a fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Lan Larison for New England.</p><p>On his only drive, Maye completed three of four passes for 48 yards. He also scrambled for 11 yards. Hutchinson sacked Maye at the Detroit 15-yard line on third down. Andy Borregales then kicked a 33-yard field goal.</p><p>New England coach Mike Vrabel he didn't know the extent of Maye's injury: "We'll have to get some more tests run and we'll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has."</p><p>After DeVito entered the game, the Patriots punted on four straight possessions. DeVito then threw an interception to Roger McCreary late in the first half. The Lions couldn't capitalize, though. Goff was picked off in the back of the end zone by Kevin Byard III.</p><p>Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez had his first interception of the season in the first half. Mack Hollins led the Patriots with five catches for 48 yards.</p><p>"We're heading into the bye and we have to get some things fixed and changed and corrected and figure out ways to win as opposed to what we're doing right now, which is not giving ourselves enough of a chance," Vrabel said.</p><h3>New field incoming</h3><h3></h3><p>Immediately after the game, workers will start installing a new field. Bayern Munich hosts Cologne on Friday night in a Bundesliga game. The NFL wouldn't confirm a German media report that said the league would pay up to 200,000 euros ($220,000) for the new pitch. In a statement to AP, the league said only that it will "work in partnership with Allianz Arena to replace the field following Sunday's game."</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Patriots:</b> Besides Maye, WR A.J. Brown left in the second half with a hamstring injury. Brown had missed the past two games with ankle and knee problems... RT Morgan Moses left in the first quarter but returned before halftime ... RB TreVeyon Henderson, who didn't make the trip, was placed on injured reserve Saturday.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Patriots:</b> Bye week.</p><p><b>Lions:</b> Host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next Sunday.<br></p>

entries.title: Workers at 3 more hotels join strike for better wages, benefits
entries.summary: <p>Hundreds of hospitality workers at three prominent Chicago hotels have joined an ongoing strike for better wages and benefits, the workers' union announced Sunday.</p><p>Workers at the Marriott Marquis, Royal Sonesta and The Wade Hotel, represented by the union UNITE HERE Local 1, walked off the job Sunday. Hundreds of others at the Sheraton Grand Chicago Riverwalk, Waldorf Astoria Chicago, Palmer House a Hilton Hotel, The Westin Chicago River North, Westin Michigan Avenue, Millennium Hotel Knickerbocker, Hilton Chicago and Hyatt Regency Chicago have been on strike already this fall, many of them since mid-October when strikes at six hotels began ahead of the Chicago Marathon.</p><p>Workers say they are overworked and not paid fairly, and they're hoping a strike prompts progress at the bargaining table.</p><p>“I don’t want to be on strike, especially with this cold weather," said Maria Jimenez, a housekeeper at the Royal Sonesta. “But this is what we have to do. We the workers keep the hotels running, and yet it isn’t enough for these companies. They’re not respecting us at the negotiating table."</p><p>Hotel employees are strapped financially, according to the union, with around one-third of members reporting they struggle to cover rent and utilities, according to a 2025 survey conducted by the union. Contracts with Hyatt, Marriott and Hilton expired Aug. 31.</p><p>Royal Sonesta and Marriott, which operates Marriott Marquis and The Wade Hotel, didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Holiday desserts for grown-ups spark controversy
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My family gathers for holidays like so many. I love making different treats, including desserts or fruit soaked in brandy. Everyone loves them, and they're kept well out of children's reach. One person is objecting to this and asking that I not bring it. They say their kids are asking why they can't have the brandied fruit, and they're uncomfortable explaining. They feel nothing should be off-limits.</p><p>I don't understand this. When I was growing up, there was always adult punch and other things we kids couldn't have. I feel the explanation is simple: Some things are for grown-ups. The hosts are afraid of causing a rift. Should we go along and let the kids be in charge, or should this be a teaching moment? — <i>ADULTS ONLY</i></p><p><b>DEAR ADULTS ONLY:</b> The simplest solution would be to make a nonalcoholic version of your dish and serve that to any minors — or abstaining adults — who express an interest. (For the record, if this parent is uncomfortable explaining the rules of modern society to their kids, I think you'd be an excellent candidate for the job.)</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I have been happily married for 32 years. Unfortunately, my wife's two sisters and her mother have rejected me. Two of the three have said so. I don't believe I have done anything wrong and have asked them why, which they refuse to reveal. They are nasty to me and falsely accuse me of being a "controlling husband" who does not let my wife go out with girlfriends. They ask my wife to choose between me and them, and they weaponize my son's hospitalization by intentionally not showing any caring.</p><p>Eight years ago, at the age of 52, I was formally diagnosed by my therapist as having autism. The in-laws said, "Had we known you were autistic, things would have been different." This was painful for me, as I don't believe in wearing medical issues or disabilities as a badge, and I think it elicits prejudice.</p><p>I believe (but cannot prove) that the reason they have rejected me is because I am not of their ethnicity, I have an introverted personality and am on the autism spectrum, or some combination. I have concluded this because my ex-brother-in-law was treated similarly. He chose a divorce and another partner with whom to move forward. I am not interested in that solution, but I am miserable.</p><p>My wife and son agree with my assessment and are supportive, but I can't find a way to move forward. Can you help? — <i>MISERABLE IN PENNSYLVANIA</i></p><p><b>DEAR MISERABLE:</b> I can try. Rather than make yourself miserable because your wife's family refuses to accept you, quit trying. A way to move forward that has worked for many other people is to start forming a "chosen" family and expose yourself as little as possible to your in-laws. A chosen family is comprised of people who like and respect you and your wife, and whose company you can enjoy without feeling judged. You may be introverted, but you do not have to be isolated.</p><p>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127. </p>

entries.title: Public health advocates call for stricter nitrate standards in drinking water
entries.summary: <p>A coalition of environmental and public health organizations are calling on federal regulators to revise the nationwide limit on toxic nitrates allowed in drinking water.</p><p>National and local advocacy groups like the Natural Resources Defense Council, Food & Water Watch, Prairie Rivers Network, and 11 others warn in the <a class="Link" href="https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28896368-epa-nitrate-petition/" target="_blank" >petition</a> submitted Monday to the U.S Environmental Protection Agency that “nitrates in drinking water are causing a public health crisis across the country.”</p><p>Nitrate is a key chemical compound common in fertilizer, which can contaminate drinking water sources. Recent studies have linked nitrate in drinking water with colorectal cancer, thyroid disease, and fetal abnormalities.</p><p>Illinois is a hot spot for nitrate pollution. Agricultural runoff can seep into groundwater and flow into streams, rivers, and reservoirs.</p><p>“One in three Americans are currently being served water with dangerous levels of nitrate in it,” said Tyler Lobdell, a senior staff attorney at Food & Water Watch.</p><p>The coalition is requesting the US EPA change the maximum contaminant level of nitrate in drinking water standard from 10 mg/L to 1 mg/liter.</p><p>“This change would reflect the best available, peer- reviewed science and would bring substantial health benefits to communities across the country,” according to the petition.</p><p>Between 2021, and 2023, more than 2 million people in Illinois were served drinking water that tested above 1 milligram of nitrate per liter, according to Robert Hirschfeld, the director of water policy at the Illinois environmental group Prairie Rivers Network.</p><p>“I would like to see this petition put the state of Illinois on notice that nitrate is a significant problem,” Hirschfeld said.</p><p>Opponents of the current federal drinking water standard for nitrate — set today at a limit of 10 milligrams per liter — worry that the decades-old benchmark is out of date.</p><p>The longstanding threshold was set as a placeholder in 1975 and formally adopted in 1991 based on the risk of blue baby syndrome, a condition in which newborns exhibit discoloration due to low levels of oxygen.</p><p>A growing body of research is pointing to additional health issues bearing down on rural America where industrial agriculture is most prevalent. Now, advocates want public health officials to adopt tougher safety standards for drinking water.</p><p>EPA has tried to reassess the nitrate benchmark twice, first under the Obama administration and then again under the Biden administration. The first and second Trump administrations scuttled both efforts.</p><p>“We've done the EPA's work for it," Lobdell said.</p><p>As part of its petition, the coalition compiled the latest science and a 43-page cost-benefit analysis to justify the stricter limit.</p><p>The petitions ask the EPA to take two immediate steps. First, the agency should institute an interim protective threshold for nitrate while they adopt a new limit. Second, they should enforce other federal protections like the Clean Water Act and rein in industrial agriculture, which Lobdell said has been given a “free pass to pollute.”</p>

entries.title: CPS overtime pay costs skyrocketed despite a 2022 warning to rein in spending
entries.summary: <p>Extra pay earned by Chicago Public Schools staff exploded in recent years after the district failed to heed some recommendations issued in 2022 that might have brought the spending under control.</p><p>That’s according to a new report from the CPS inspector general’s office, released Monday. The inspector general found the school district’s overtime costs tripled from 2019 to a peak of $150 million in 2024. In 2025, the most recent year examined by the OIG, the amount dropped to $97 million.</p><p>“When it goes unmonitored and untracked, it can absolutely lead to fraud and waste, we've seen it in our investigations over the years,” Inspector General Philip Wagenknecht said. “We’ve had cases where clerks are involved in paying themselves over time. Several years ago, we had a principal who was indicted and convicted for a phony extra pay scheme where she was distributing the pay to her staff and requiring them to kick it back to her.”</p><p>Wagenknecht’s office found issues with extra pay to employees among a range of positions and parts of CPS but found particularly high levels among custodians. One custodian, for example, punched in and out of work for 77 days in a row, including weekends.</p><p>CPS officials say they take the Inspector General’s findings “seriously and are continuing to strengthen controls over extra pay, including overtime, extended day and stipends. The District will continue to review and update guidance and monitor payroll procedures.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-100000" name="html-embed-module-100000"></a><div style="min-height:540px" id="datawrapper-vis-1qN4z"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/1qN4z/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-1qN4z"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/1qN4z/full.png" alt="Spending on extra pay at CPS has increased dramatically since 2019 (Column Chart)" /></noscript></div> </div> </div><p>The report comes as the school district has had to cut to close budget deficits for the past three years and is expected to face one again this coming year.</p><p>The inspector general’s report is a follow-up to one in 2022 that pointed out the district lacked controls on extra pay and expressed concern that “spending might continue to rise unchecked, especially with federal COVID relief funding available.” CPS received $2.8 billion in COVID-19 relief funds, which it had to spend by the end of 2025.</p><p>“Unfortunately, the OIG’s prediction came true,” the inspector general wrote in the report, referring to the Office of the Inspector General.</p><p>In response to the report, CPS officials say they have or are working on implementing some of the recommendations. These include capping what employees can earn in a given period through what’s known as “extended day pay” and creating a system to monitor whether protocols are being followed.</p><p>The OIG examined different types of extra pay: traditional overtime for hourly workers, typically 1.5 times their rate; and extended day pay, which is paid by the hour; and lump-sum stipends, which are two categories of pay teachers and other staff can earn for work done outside their standard schedule, like running a club or a sport.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-d50000" name="html-embed-module-d50000"></a><div style="min-height:538px" id="datawrapper-vis-SUro7"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/SUro7/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-SUro7"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/SUro7/full.png" alt="How CPS doled out extra pay in the 2025 fiscal year (Pie Chart)" /></noscript></div> </div> </div><p>CPS put aside more than $100 million in COVID-relief money for extended day payments as the district sought to recoup learning loss and increase attendance through after-school programs.</p><p>Yet the inspector general noted, back in 2022, the deployment of those extra pay dollars was ripe for fraud and CPS did not have limits, accepted paperwork without proper approvals and did not monitor it to catch excessive payments.</p><p>And the inspector general’s new report details a number of situations where employees appeared to collect a lot of extra pay without questions. For example, over four years, six employees made $200,000 in extra pay and 147 made $100,000 in extra pay.</p><p>The facilities department and its custodians received the most overtime pay in each of the years the inspector general reviewed. His office noted the costs in 2025 might be a result of the district laying off 160 custodians who clean schools. CPS kept all the 1,225 custodians employed by the district. This resulted in a 6% drop in custodian positions.</p><p>Even if there was more work to do, some of the extra pay for custodians was exorbitant, the report said. One custodian took home $275,000 in extra pay over four years. Another earned $81,000, in addition to a regular salary of $61,000, in 2025.</p><p>CPS noted in 2025 the management of custodians was in transition as the district took it over after it had been privatized for more than a decade.</p>

a dead-serious patty-cake game called “Kid Gunner Brother”; and a piece by former Chicagoan Alex Temple called “Ah yes, the three genders,” in reference to an internet meme. Here, instead of referring to found alignments of three items such as printed guides prominently labeled “girl,” “boy” and “mischief,” the title refers to the percussion-instrument classifications of wood, metal and skins.</p><p>A piece called “Golden Gate,” a vibraphone-marimba duet that manages to sound both insistent and meditative, has a memorable origin. The composer, Kevin Rosacia, wrote it as an ode to what the city of San Francisco has meant to gay culture and about building a bridge to connect himself with the LGBTQ community. Spectrum plays only the music of queer composers. When the ensemble put out a call for commissions, Rosacia responded, even though he wasn’t yet out.</p><p>“So he used this as his coming-out piece,” Esposito said, “which was pretty inspiring and special for us to be able to do.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-a50000" name="image-a50000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/280e327/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F6c%2F3a%2Fb31d34e549cfa2894d59cd073c65%2Fspectrum-261115-10.png 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/e0541db/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F6c%2F3a%2Fb31d34e549cfa2894d59cd073c65%2Fspectrum-261115-10.png 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b0fe72d/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F6c%2F3a%2Fb31d34e549cfa2894d59cd073c65%2Fspectrum-261115-10.png" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Jaime Esposito of Spectrum Ensemble performs during the Going Dutch Festival at Side Street Studio Arts in Elgin on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. The title is a reference to the shibboleth “friend of Dorothy,” which gay people used to identify one another in the mid-20th century. Another Dorothy fragment calls for a death drop, a dance move from drag culture where the dancer falls suddenly to a supine position with one leg folded underneath. “Luckily, that’s Cleo’s part,” Esposito said. (Elsewhere in their performance life, Goldberg performs as the drag queen Manic Maxxie.)</p><p>Clearly, the normal protocols of classical-tradition concertgoing are out the window. “Like the concert black, we don’t play that game,” Esposito said. “We wear jumpsuits with rainbows and our names on the back, because it doesn’t need to be that serious.”</p><p>Goldberg’s first appearance with Spectrum came during the COVID-19 pandemic, when Manic Maxxie cameoed in full glam to do the death drop routine in an online performance of “Dorothy Fragments.” Goldberg and Esposito knew each other from percussion symposia and past festivals, dating to when Goldberg was in high school and Esposito attended Northwestern. So when Esposito moved back to Chicago in January for a day-job opportunity, they invited Goldberg to team up to re-establish the duo.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-700000" name="image-700000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/1dd671b/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a49dfd4/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a80fd45/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Spectrum Ensemble consisting of Jaime Esposito and Cleo Goldberg perform during the Going Dutch Festival at Side Street Studio Arts in Elgin on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a80fd45/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b4643a6/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a80fd45/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>The duo sees good things ahead for Spectrum now that it’s based in Chicago.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Mark Black for the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>It’s a complementary partnership. Esposito does the administration, arranging bookings and grants, and serving as the outward-facing half of the duo. Goldberg takes on the most technically difficult music. “When [Esposito] first pitched joining the ensemble to me, they said to me, ‘You’re the talent. I’m the business,’” Goldberg said. “I actually said, ‘Jaime, you are also the talent!’”</p><p>The duo sees good things ahead for Spectrum now that it’s based in Chicago. “We didn’t really get gigs in Texas very often, unless it was, like, Fort Worth Pride,” Esposito said. “So I really hope this just creates a lot of opportunity.”</p><p>They’ve already booked a partnership with groups called Trans Composers Project and Queer Music Midwest for 45 minutes of newly commissioned music for percussion duo, scheduled for premiere in March 2027, tentatively in Chicago.</p><p>It promises to be a showcase for the queer music community in its full fabulousness, a community that is here making art for everyone all the time — not just during Pride Month.</p>

entries.summary: <p>Illinois lawmakers will line up in Springfield this week for their goal line stand to block the Chicago Bears from rushing off to Indiana.</p><p>At least, that’s the game plan heading into the fall veto session, as legislators hope to finally pass a bill to help the team build a new stadium in their home state — whether that’s in Arlington Heights or the city the Bears have represented for more than a century.</p><p>Gov. JB Pritzker and his General Assembly allies have expressed <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/10/19/chicago-bears-stadium-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-gubernatorial-election-arlington-heights-chicago-indiana" target="_blank" ><u>as much confidence as ever</u></a> that the Bears’ five-year stadium flirtation is nearing a conclusion.</p><p>But the team remains as noncommittal as ever, weighing its suburban option versus two potential sites in Hammond, Indiana, plus a parade of revamped Chicago-based proposals the Bears have previously dismissed.</p><p>While that political football will eat up much of the Capitol play clock beginning Tuesday, legislators will also make a drive to pass new regulations on data centers, and even more tussling will happen behind closed doors as House Democrats maneuver to succeed outgoing Speaker Emanuel “Chris” Welch.</p><p>The first week of session is scheduled through Thursday before lawmakers finish out their calendar Dec. 1-3. Here’s what to watch for:</p><h3><b>Bears back on the clock</b></h3><p>Momentum has built behind one of the two Illinois bills that emerged in a frenzied but fruitless stadium push <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/05/31/bears-stadium-bill-springfield-arlington-heights-hammond-indiana" target="_blank" ><u>late in the spring session</u></a>, the most recent Springfield shutout that prompted the Bears to publicly shift their focus to Hammond.</p><p>With stadium negotiators all but trashing the framework the Bears had long sought — discounted payments in lieu of taxes to local governments (PILOT) — the sides have coalesced behind a municipal stadium authority model that would allow Chicago and Arlington Heights to lure the Bears and negotiate terms of a publicly owned stadium.</p><p>“There has been good progress made on a bill that would create a site-neutral and franchise-neutral approach to settling the stadium question,” said state Sen. Bill Cunningham, the South Side Democrat who serves as his chamber’s top stadium negotiator.</p><p>Cunningham spearheaded the initial version of the bill that passed the Senate but never got a House vote in the waning overnight hours of the spring session.</p><p>The municipal authority model gives Chicago a shot at keeping the Bears — and perhaps more importantly, gives Chicago legislators political cover to support a bill that could ultimately send the team to the suburbs.</p><p>While evaluating the Hammond sites — and testing the patience of Hoosier lawmakers who rolled out the navy-and-orange carpet with a generous taxpayer-funded stadium law signed <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/02/26/bears-stadium-hammond-indiana-hammong-senate-passes-bill-27-arlington-heights-george-mccaaskey-kevin-warren-nfl" target="_blank" ><u>in February</u></a> — the Bears’ Illinois talks have progressed since bringing minority owner Pat Ryan and NFL commissioner <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/06/bears-stadium-roger-goodell-nfl-commissioner-george-mccaskey-kevin-warren-chicago-arlington-heights-meeting-hammond-indiana" target="_blank" ><u>Roger Goodell</u></a> to the table over the summer.</p><p>Not that Illinois leaders are anywhere near victory formation. Negotiators don’t expect to vote on a bill until the second half of the session — and wouldn’t be surprised if it gets punted to the lame-duck session after the holidays.</p><p>“Getting agreement between all the parties is less important than getting members of the General Assembly comfortable with any kind of approach,” Cunningham said. “That’s the consensus that has to occur.”</p><p>A Bears spokesman pointed to the team’s most recent declaration they “appreciate the recent engagement from Illinois leadership” and “expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams [including Indiana] in the coming weeks.”</p><p>The team still has reservations about the state's commitment to funding public infrastructure upgrades around a potential stadium, upwards of $800 million that would be doled out incrementally over several state budget cycles. Meanwhile, suburban officials in Palatine and Rolling Meadows are demanding a seat at the table for Arlington Heights' potential municipal stadium authority, since their towns would neighbor the dome.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-710000" name="image-710000"></a> <picture on the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/other-views/2026/06/22/bears-south-side-hammond-should-beat-arlington-heights-nfl-state-rep-curtis-tarver" target="_blank" ><u>Southeast href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/10/28/bridgeport-bears-domed-stadium-proposal-sox-rate-field" target="_blank" ><u>Bridgeport</u></a>.</p><p>Yet another proposal unaffiliated with the team is expected to surface soon, a revamped take on the lakefront dome south of Soldier Field the Bears <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2024/04/23/bears-new-stadium-dome-lakefront-soldier-field" target="_blank" ><u>pitched in 2024</u></a> with Mayor Brandon Johnson but was almost immediately shot down by Springfield due to its hefty public price tag.</p><p>Johnson’s office hasn’t yet endorsed a specific city proposal, but the “bottom line is that the mayor knows that Chicago is and should remain the home of the Bears and will continue to work with stakeholders across the region to make it so,” a spokesperson said in an email.</p><h3><b>Dealing with data centers</b></h3><p>Aside from Bears legislation, Gov. Pritzker said his top veto session agenda item is passing new data center regulations amid increasing concerns over data centers' impact on residential water and energy bills.</p><p>He and his General Assembly allies will aim to pass the Protecting Our Water, Energy and Ratepayers Act, or <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/10/22/data-centers-comed-3-billion-icc-consumer-groups-cub-illinois-households" target="_blank" ><u>POWER Act</u></a>, which would require data center developers to pay 100% of their costs before connecting to the grid. The bill languished at the end of May.</p><p>“We have a bill that would curtail the use of any outside electricity, and instead require data centers to bring their own electricity with them — clean energy, and also require them to use closed water systems,” Pritzker said earlier this month. “It should be up to local communities, whether or not they want a data center.”</p><h3><b>Speaker’s race</b></h3><p>The election’s over, but the politicking hasn’t stopped behind the scenes following Speaker Welch’s announcement he won’t seek a fourth term with the gavel, in the wake of a mutiny of caucus members who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/11/12/illinois-house-speaker-emanuel-chris-welch-accusations-domestic-abuse-lawsuits-patronage-proviso-district" target="_blank" ><u>criticized</u></a> his handling of sexual harassment allegations against ex-state Rep. Harry Benton.</p><p>Several <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/springfield/2026/11/06/illinois-house-speaker-chris-welch-steps-down-female-replacement-contenders" target="_blank" ><u>ambitious House Democrats</u></a> are already making calls to their colleagues seeking their support, though it’s not clear when a vote will happen to select the supermajority caucus’ leader come January, when the 105th General Assembly is sworn in.</p><p>Downtown state Rep. Kam Buckner has publicly<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/fran-spielman-show/2026/11/11/kam-buckner-illinois-house-speaker-candidate-emanuel-chris-welch-ouster-harry-benton" > tossed his hat </a>in the ring, while other clout-heavy names are being floated, including state Reps. Eva-Dina Delgado, Jehan Gordon-Booth, Lisa Hernandez, Ann Williams, Marcus Evans and Jay Hoffman.</p>

entries.title: Voter turnout dropped in Chicago's GOP strongholds, increased in areas affected by Operation Midway Blitz
entries.summary: <p>Traditional Republican strongholds in Chicago saw a decrease in voter turnout in the Nov. 3 election, while areas affected by Operation Midway Blitz saw a bump.</p><p>WBEZ and the Chicago Sun-Times examined the 90 precincts President Donald Trump won in 2024, which represent traditionally conservative areas of the city. Voter turnout in those precincts was down an average of 6.26 percentage points in the November election compared to 2022.</p><p>And traditionally Democratic precincts that voted for Kamala Harris saw an increase in voter turnout by an average of 3.23 percentage points.</p><p>The analysis is based on election results posted by the Chicago Board of Election Commissioners as of Friday afternoon.</p><p>At the same time, data shows voter turnout was up in neighborhoods affected by Operation Midway Blitz, including in Little Village, Pilsen, Humboldt Park and the South Shore neighborhood. During the height of the immigration enforcement, 3,841 people were detained. Only 15% of those detained had a criminal conviction.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-400000" name="html-embed-module-400000"></a><div class="cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper"> <div class="cpm-gfx-embed"> <div style="min-height:789px" id="datawrapper-vis-DlEku"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/DlEku/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-DlEku"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/DlEku/full.png" alt="Choropleth map" /></noscript></div> </div> <div class="cpm-gfx-embed"> <div style="min-height:772px" id="datawrapper-vis-yoOWW"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/yoOWW/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-yoOWW"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/yoOWW/full.png" alt="Choropleth map" /></noscript></div> </div> </div> <style> .cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper { align-items: start; display: flex; flex-direction: row; gap: 2rem; } .cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper .cpm-gfx-embed { flex: 1; min-width: 18rem; } @media screen and (max-width: 30rem) { .cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper { align-items: stretch; flex-direction: column; gap: 0; } } </style> </div> </div><p>In the South Shore raid on Sept. 30, 2025, allegedly acting on a <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/housing/2026/01/22/residents-long-suspected-feds-south-shore-raid-tip-came-from-landlord-now-under-state-investigation-immigration-bovino-border-patrol-ice" target="_blank" ><u>tip from building management</u></a>, federal agents rappelled down from helicopters, ransacked the building and zip-tied residents, many of them U.S. citizens. Government officials said they were going after members of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, but no criminal charges have been filed against anyone arrested that night.</p><p>In the 7th Ward, where federal agents raided the South Shore building, voter turnout was up 5.3 percentage points.</p><p>In Little Village and surrounding neighborhoods, home to the 22nd Ward, all precincts saw an increase in voter turnout except for the precinct that is home to the Cook County Jail, which saw a drop of 6.5 percentage points compared to the 2022 midterms. Trump won that precinct in 2024. All precincts in Pilsen also saw increases in voter turnout.</p><p>All precincts in the 41st Ward on the Far Northwest Side also saw drops in voter turnout. The ward was the only in which Trump won more than half the votes in the November 2024 election.</p><p>Nearly all precincts in the 19th Ward, home to Beverly and Mount Greenwood, saw a double digit drop in voter turnout in the November election. The neighborhoods, home to police officers, firefighters and union workers, have historically shown support for GOP candidates.</p><h3><b>Blue gains across Illinois</b></h3><p>In Chicago, Trump jumped to 22.01% of the city vote in 2024, up from 12.41% of the city vote in 2016. In Illinois, Trump’s statewide vote grew to 45.3% in 2024, up from 38.76% in 2016, according to returns.</p><p>But the November election painted a picture of national dissatisfaction over Trump administration policies, including the war in Iran, which has directly impacted gas prices, as well as aggressive immigration efforts and general affordability issues affecting Americans.</p><p>With Democratic blowouts in favor of Gov. JB Pritzker, Attorney General Kwame Raoul, Comptroller-elect Margaret Croke and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/03/governor-illinois-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett-results" target="_blank" ><u>all other statewide officeholders</u></a>, Illinois Republicans are finding themselves in dire straits.</p><p>Democrats even made inroads in territory long considered solid Republican ground, with Ricky Rivard unseating four-term GOP St. Charles state Rep. Dan Ugaste.</p><p>Rockford state Sen. Dave Syverson — the longest-serving member of the chamber, in office since 1993 — narrowly won against Democratic challenger Sarah Mertens, 50.8% to 49.2%.</p><p>Pritzker won his third term by his widest margin yet — 60.6% to Darren Bailey’s 36%. The Democratic governor also picked up red counties like Winnebago, McHenry, Sangamon and Jackson counties.</p><h3><b>Operation Midway Blitz a motivating factor</b></h3><p>Growing up in Little Village, Brenda Anaya said she grew accustomed to seeing the neighborhood bustling with people. But that changed when the Trump administration launched Operation Midway Blitz last fall.</p><p>As federal agents began filling the streets in search of undocumented immigrants, Anaya said residents grew fearful and stopped leaving their homes.</p><p>“A lot of people were scared,” said Anaya, 27. “It was a hard time for everyone living here.”</p><p>Anaya voted for Democrats in the midterm election and was confident they would win in Illinois. However, she was surprised to see Democratic victories extend beyond the state and across the country.</p><p>After Democrats gained control of both the U.S. Senate and U.S. House of Representatives during the midterm elections, Anaya said she’s beginning to hope things will return to normal.</p><p>“When [elected officials] come into office, I hope they do what they can to stop ICE,” she said.</p><p>Anaya hopes immigration enforcement will stop not only in Chicago but across the country.</p><p>“People should feel safe,” she said.</p>
